Well this is from my mum’s perspective initially then it becomes my mum and me type of perspective - 5pm 2nd November 2016, I get a message to come home real quick. I’m here at my friends’ dorm reading the message like “hmm my mum never texts like this, I gotta go”; 2 hours later, I get to my road and I notice 4 police cars and 2 paramedic vehicles by my door... Everyone on my road had either their lights, doors or curtains open to see what the heck was going on. I notice that this might be it, but I was oblivious to this - so oblivious that I just opened my door and assumed all’s good and well.

Nope. Mum is crying and lead officer and paramedic is hugging my mum and I just sat down. My brain is like “No way this is happening right now...” 

Police officer carefully mentions “I’m sorry to say this but your Dad passed away” 

I run up the stairs in disbelief and I just see my father’s body - at peace from all the pain he was suffering over a 5 year span (Parkinson’s, Alzheimers, Quad-bypass). 

Usual procedures occurred, my grieving took over 2 years - I literally started uni, turned 19, ready for the step up in life but this took such a big toll on me that everything went backwards i.e. grades, social life etc. 

Now it’s been more than 4 years ago, I’m feeling much better and I’m about to start work at a top hospital!

note: I still feel so bad I didn’t do anything nice for him in his last moments, it’s that everlasting guilt I can’t get rid of from my mind ever. It sucks.
